protections: IN_PLACE: every node the sanitizer detaches from the caller's live tree is stripped of non-allowlisted attributes before sanitize returns, via the end-of-walk harvest of DOMPurify.removed into _neutralizeSubtree/_stripDisallowedAttributes (src/purify.ts:2528-2546, src/purify.ts:1310-1328, src/purify.ts:1267-1286).

IN_PLACE + KEEP_CONTENT: the original children of a disallowed wrapper are hoisted back into the walk instead of being left detached as clones, so the nodes that carry already-queued resource events are the ones sanitized (src/purify.ts:1701-1739).

IN_PLACE abort: a mid-walk exception empties the caller's live root so it is not returned half-sanitized, and the original error is rethrown (src/purify.ts:1190-1220, src/purify.ts:2432-2438, src/purify.ts:2519-2525).
IN_PLACE entry: a forbidden or DOM-clobbered root is refused with a throw instead of being sanitized or neutralized (src/purify.ts:2402-2425).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Hooks are the application's own trusted code and the node is gone from the returned tree, so the output looks clean; the only argument for leaving it is that a hook which removes a node is executing the caller's instruction.

The report describes a hook removing the node it was called on; a hook that reaches out and removes an ancestor, a sibling or a child is a different shape, hooks are trusted, and the node the hook was invoked with was neutralized, so the fix looks complete.
This is only the abort path: the call throws, the in-place root is emptied so the caller's tree looks fail-closed, and the children were detached rather than left rendered.
A hook that calls sanitize again is exotic app behaviour, the nested call looks self-contained, and its own harvest is assumed to tidy up the removals.
Shadow content is assumed inert (template.content is), and the IN_PLACE pre-pass already sanitized the shadow root, so a hook removal there looks harmless.

masking: T1 masks T2, T3 and T4: while hook removals are silently unneutralised, the removed-list harvest (src/purify.ts:2536-2540) looks like complete coverage, so the ancestor/sibling shape, the abort teardown and the re-entrancy bookkeeping are never exercised.

T1's natural per-node fix masks T2: a check on the hook's currentNode (parentless) fires for the reported shape but not for an ancestor removal, where currentNode keeps its parent and the detached armed subtree is a different object.

T3 is masked by the throw contract: the caller sees an exception, so the children _neutralizeRoot detaches raw (including the armed in the C3-F2 fixture, test/test-suite.js:5615-5626) are never inspected.

conflicts.what: A per-node check on the hook's currentNode (T1's natural fix) is exactly what leaves the ancestor/sibling shape of T2 open; widening it to a containment test over the iterator root pulls in <template>.content and attached shadow-root nodes, which are not childNodes descendants of the root and whose hook-added attributes must survive in the output, so the T2 fix has to add template/shadow walking while T1's minimal fix does not.

Fixing T4 by keeping the removal list local to each sanitize call leaves _neutralizeRoot (T3) with no list of its own: the abort barrier detaches children itself, so neutralization has to happen at the point of detach, whereas T4's fix pushes toward an end-of-call harvest - the two fixes disagree about when neutralization happens.

fairness_risks: Documented node-removing hooks must keep working: demos/hooks-node-removal-demo.html:20-25 removes empty nodes in beforeSanitizeAttributes and demos/hooks-node-removal2-demo.html:49-53 removes a <footer> in uponSanitizeElement; a rule that throws on, or refuses, any hook-detached node contradicts documented behaviour.

DOMPurify.removed is a public inventory (src/types.ts:19-23) that callers and tests read (test/test-suite.js:1538-1547), even though README.md:86 warns against security use; a fix that stops recording removals or rebinds the array breaks observable behaviour.

Attributes a hook adds to kept nodes are documented as not re-validated (test/test-suite.js:3272-3288); a blanket 'strip everything that left the root' rule must not reach nodes that are in the output, including all of <template>.content and attached shadow roots, which are not descendants of the root through childNodes.

A clobbered or forbidden IN_PLACE root must still throw rather than be neutralized (test/test-suite.js:1461-1474, test/test-suite.js:4771-4792); a rule that requires the live tree to be neutralized on every exit would contradict that documented refusal contract.
Refused input shape: a hook that removes an empty element (the documented demo) is a legitimate shape that a 'hooks may not detach nodes' rule would reject.

design.why: Four independent sites with four different dismissals. T1 is the reported route and is the warm-up: a hook detaches the current node, the iterator's next step resumes after the detached subtree, no handler in that subtree is ever stripped, and the node never enters DOMPurify.removed, so the return-path harvest (src/purify.ts:2536-2540) cannot see it. T2 is the wrong-object case: a hook that detaches an ancestor, sibling or child leaves the node the hook was invoked with parented, so the natural 'is currentNode still parented?' guard reports success; closing it needs containment reasoning against the iterator root, which then has to be extended to template.content and shadow roots or it strips nodes that ARE in the output. T3 is the far-site case with the strongest dismissal ('we throw, so we failed closed'): _neutralizeRoot empties the root but detaches its children raw (src/purify.ts:1197 vs 1206), so the armed of the existing C3-F2 fixture survives - a DeepSeek-type trap. T4 is the bookkeeping case: a re-entrant sanitize from inside a hook replaces DOMPurify.removed (src/purify.ts:2383), so everything the outer walk detached before the nested call is never harvested - a how-type mechanism MiMo tends to miss. T5 (hook removal inside the shadow walk) is grouped with T1 because a guard placed in _sanitizeAttributes, which _sanitizeShadowDOM also calls (src/purify.ts:2188-2191), closes both; only a main-walk-only guard leaves it open. This design beats the one-guard alternatives: a single tree-diff guard is heavier, has to special-case template.content/shadow roots or over-strip documented hook-added attributes, and still needs a separate answer for the abort barrier and for the re-entrant call.

History encoding: b_in_code_a_wrote=true records that the later gap is in the coverage of the neutralisation code the earlier fix added (src/purify.ts:2536-2540) - an incomplete fix, not a regression; the detach itself happens at the older hook call sites (src/purify.ts:1825, src/purify.ts:2168).

Queued-event execution is not observable in this checkout (the node harness uses jsdom/happy-dom, which do not load resources), so traps are stated as attribute invariants (the captured original keeps or loses its on* handler), matching what the existing audit-5 and C3-F2 tests assert (test/test-suite.js:5412-5448, test/test-suite.js:5626-5631).

T4's precondition (a hook calling DOMPurify.sanitize re-entrantly) is exercised nowhere in the suite; src/purify.ts:242-258 shows re-entrancy is a considered scenario for Trusted Types policies, but no test calls sanitize from inside a hook.

The entry-refusal paths (src/purify.ts:2402-2425) also exit with the caller's live tree still armed, but are not listed as traps because the throw is the documented refusal contract (test/test-suite.js:1461-1474, test/test-suite.js:4771-4792); whether a hidden test would want neutralisation there is unknown.
